blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Geometric structure is essential for robotic manipulation and understanding the 3D world. Most VLA models rely on 2D representations of current observations, while geometry-aware approaches often require additional 3D information. However, geometry inferred independently from individual observations is often discarded rather than accumulated into a persistent task representation. Our key insight is that action generation needs a compact, task-relevant geometric abstraction that can be continuously updated, rather than a complete, renderable 3D reconstruction at every step. We introduce GeoMem-VLA, a VLA framework that internalizes explicit 3D supervision into dedicated geometric tokens and maintains them as temporal memory for action generation, without directly aligning the VLM's native visual embeddings with the teacher feature space. During training, a frozen geometry foundation model supervises learnable GeoPlan tokens through a geometric flow-matching objective over the current scene point map and future end-effector tracks. These tokens are integrated with the memory of observation representations, where historical information is retrieved, adaptively fused with current observations, and consolidated to retain event frames as the task progresses. At inference, the policy retrieves historical representations and fuses them with the current working representation to predict actions, without invoking the 3D teacher or explicitly reconstructing the scene. After benchmark-specific downstream adaptation, GeoMem-VLA achieves 98.9% average success on LIBERO and 91.10% / 91.24% on RoboTwin's clean/randomized settings. Across five real-world tasks, GeoMem-VLA achieves 78.0% average success. These results suggest that internalizing and remembering 3D scene understanding is a promising approach to robot control.
blocks.zh: 几何结构对于机器人操纵和理解3D世界至关重要. 大多数VLA模型依赖于当前观测的2D表示,而几何-知觉方法往往需要额外的3D信息. 然而,从个别观察中独立推断出来的几何往往被抛弃,而不是被累积成一个持续的任务表述. 我们的主要见解是,行动生成需要一种紧凑的、与任务相关的几何抽象,这种抽象可以不断更新,而不是在每一个步骤上进行完整的、可转换的三维重建。 我们引入了GeoMem-VLA,这是一个VLA框架,将明确的3D监督内化为专用几何符号,并保持它们作为动作生成的时间记忆,而不会直接将VLM的原生视觉嵌入与老师的特有空间相配合. 在训练期间,一个被冻结的几何地基模型通过一个几何相容的目标,对可学习的地平规划符号进行监督,该目标将覆盖目前的地平线地平线地平线和未来的终点效应轨道。 这些标志与观测表达的内存相融合,其中历史信息被检索,适应性地与当前观测相融合,并被合并,以保留随着任务进展的事件帧. 推论,政策取回了历史表述,并将其与目前的工作表述相融合,以预测行动,而无需引用3D老师或明确重建场景. 在具体基准下游适应后,GeoMem-VLA在LIBERO上取得了98.9%的平均成功,在RoboTwin的清洁/随机设置上取得了91.10%/91.24%的平均成功. 在五个现实世界的任务中,GeoMem-VLA取得了78.0%的平均成功. 这些结果表明,对3D场景的内化和记忆理解是机器人控制的一种有希望的方法.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Robotic manipulation requires combining semantic understanding with precise
3D control. Building on advances in large language models, vision-language-action
(VLA) models have attracted attention for language-conditioned manipulation ( Brohan et al., 2023 ; Kim et al., 2024 ; Black et al., 2024 ; Shi et al., 2026b ) . Most use pretrained vision-language models (VLMs)
for visual and semantic understanding and generate actions through tokenized
prediction or dedicated action experts. However, their reliance on current
2D observations offers limited support
for precise 3D spatial reasoning and decision-making that depend on
interaction history.

Recent work on 3D-aware VLAs has explored how to leverage the rich geometric priors of the physical environment ( Li et al., 2026a ; Qian et al., 2026 ) .
Such supervision allows explicit geometric targets to shape policy representations
that require explicit reconstruction during action inference.
Memory-augmented
policies, meanwhile, retain perceptual and task context from earlier
observations ( Shi et al., 2026a ) . Connecting these directions raises a central
question: How can geometric supervision shape spatial memory that guides action? This places the spatial content of memory at the center of
policy representation learning.

blocks.en:
We propose GeoMem-VLA , a VLA framework that couples geometry-supervised
GeoPlan representations with causal episode-level memory. During training,
learnable GeoPlan tokens summarize the multimodal context and condition an
auxiliary flow-matching head that predicts current-scene point maps and
future Cartesian end-effector tracks. A frozen VGGT teacher ( Wang et al., 2025 ) provides scene-geometry targets, while demonstration trajectories provide
future motion supervision. These complementary targets train the tokens to
encode scene structure and task-related motion. At deployment, the teacher
and reconstruction head are removed from the action-generation path;
the learned tokens provide compact geometric context for the policy.

To preserve this context, we maintain geometric memory alongside
perceptual and task-related memory. Current representations retrieve
relevant preceding features, and adaptive fusion integrates historical
context before action generation. Similarity-based consolidation compresses redundant entries while retaining feature-distinct temporal states. We further use event-aware
training that samples temporally separated observations from the same
episode while preserving their chronological order and causal access.
This exposes retrieval to a broader span of interaction history than
contexts formed only from neighboring frames. Together, geometric
supervision and temporal retrieval connect what the policy learns about
the scene with what it can retain for later decisions.

Our evaluation examines spatial understanding, long-horizon decision-making,
and applicability across manipulation tasks. On LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0, GeoMem-VLA achieves 98.9 % 98.9\% average success across the four LIBERO suites
and 91.10 % 91.10\% / 91.24 % 91.24\% on RoboTwin Clean / Randomized. Complementary
real-world protocols target geometric alignment and long-horizon
interaction, connecting the evaluation to the spatial and temporal
requirements of the architecture.

Our contributions are summarized as follows: • Geometry-Supervised Spatial Representations. We learn compact GeoPlan tokens from current-scene point maps and future
end-effector tracks, providing geometric conditioning without explicit
reconstruction during action inference. • Geometry-Aware Event Memory. We couple geometric representations with causally temporal retrieval and
train event-aware memory to retain key information alongside
perceptual and task context. • Evaluation Across Manipulation Settings. Experiments of geometry-supervised memory across diverse tasks through LIBERO, RoboTwin and real-world manipulation tasks examine geometric precision and the use of historical context in long-horizon manipulation.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Advances in VLMs ( Liu et al., 2024 ; Karamcheti et al., 2024 ) have enabled VLAs through robot-data scaling, vision-language pretraining,
and expressive action decoders. RT-1 ( Brohan et al., 2022 ) scales multitask learning
on demonstrations; RT-2 ( Brohan et al., 2023 ) and OpenVLA ( Kim et al., 2024 ) transfer
pretrained knowledge to discrete action prediction. π 0 \pi_{0} ( Black et al., 2024 ) ,
CogACT ( Li et al., 2024a ) , and GR00T ( Bjorck et al., 2025 ) use continuous action
experts, while π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} ( Intelligence et al., 2025 ) adds heterogeneous data and
semantic subtask prediction for open-world generalization. FAST ( Pertsch et al., 2025 ) compresses action sequences via frequency-domain
tokenization; OpenVLA-OFT ( Kim et al., 2025 ) uses parallel decoding and
action chunking for efficient execution. StarVLA ( Community, 2026 ) provides a modular backbone–expert framework. These advances leave
open how task-relevant 3D structure should be encoded and retained
across decisions.

History-aware policies use recurrent states, visual prompts, and
retrievable memory. RoboFlamingo ( Li et al., 2024b ) aggregates
sequential features with a recurrent policy head; TraceVLA ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) encodes tracked motion as visual traces. HAMLET ( Koo et al., 2026 ) aggregates distinctive moment tokens in a lightweight
memory module. MemoryVLA ( Shi et al., 2026a ) retrieves, adaptively fuses,
and consolidates perceptual and cognitive history; EventVLA ( Yang et al., 2026a ) predicts keyframes to preserve sparse visual evidence.
BridgeVLA++ ( Li et al., 2026c ) combines temporal observation history
with explicit point-cloud spatial memory. These designs trade retained
detail against temporal coverage and cost, but how scene and motion
targets shape latent history for later decisions remains open. We focus
on jointly learning and using spatial representations across time to
guide manipulation.

blocks.en:
We conduct real-world experiments to evaluate GeoMem-VLA in manipulation scenarios involving geometric reasoning and temporal context.
Specifically, we design five tasks with distinct spatial and sequential requirements as shown in Figure 4 : pick and stand sticks , transfer cup across the rack , separate file pockets on the Astribot S1 platform and pick n times cube , cover and find the apple under towel on the AgileX platform.
We collect 60 demonstrations per task and GeoMem-VLA is compared to representative VLA baselines, including LingBot-VLA 2.0 ( Wu et al., 2026b ) , π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} ( Intelligence et al., 2025 ) , and OpenVLA-OFT ( Kim et al., 2025 ) , under the same evaluation protocol.
During evaluation, we conduct 10 independent rollouts for each task under randomized object configurations and report the success rate.

我们进行现实世界的实验,在涉及几何推理和时间背景的操纵情景中评价GeoMem-VLA.
具体地说,我们设计了五个任务,其空间和顺序要求各不相同,如图4所示:取出并站起棒子,跨架转出杯子,在Astribot S1平台上单独取出文件口袋并取出n倍立方体,覆盖并找到AgileX平台上毛巾下的苹果.
我们每个任务收集60个演示,GeoMem-VLA与具有代表性的VLA基线进行比较,包括LingBot-VLA 2.0(Wu等,2026b), ^ 0.5\pi_{0.5}(Intelligence等,2025),以及OpenVLA-OFT(Kim等,2025),根据同样的评价协议.
在评价期间,我们根据随机对象配置对每项任务进行10次独立推广,并报告成功率。

blocks.en:
Figure 4 shows that GeoMem-VLA achieves robust performance across five real-world manipulation tasks.
Specifically, for comprehensive long-horizon manipulation tasks, including pick and stand sticks , transfer a cup across the rack , and cover and find the apple , GeoMem-VLA achieves 90%, 70%, and 80% success rates.
These tasks require both precise spatial interaction and maintaining task-relevant context throughout multi-stage execution, such as in pick and stand sticks task, the robot needs to repeatedly identify individual sticks, grasp them from a shared workspace, and place them into a precise upright configuration.
The results show that the geometry-supervised representations provide spatially grounded features for reliable grasping and placement, while the historical geometric context effectively maintains task progress.
Moreover, for the spatially precise separate file pockets task, GeoMem-VLA achieves 100% success rate by accurately distinguishing and manipulating the target file pocket among cluttered stacked configurations.
For pick n times cube , the challenge is maintaining progress over repeated interactions. The policy needs to remember how many successful grasp-and-place cycles have been completed while adapting to the current scene. The temporal memory mechanism preserves task progress across repeated operations, allowing GeoMem-VLA to complete the required number of interactions.

这些任务既需要精确的空间交互,又需要在整个多阶段执行中保持与任务相关的上下文,例如在接棒和站棒任务中,机器人需要反复识别出单个棒子,从共享的工作空间中抓住它们,并把它们置于精确的直立配置中.
结果显示,由几何学监督的表达方式为可靠地把握和定位提供了空间基础特征,而历史几何学背景则有效地维持了任务进展.
此外,对于空间精确的相隔文件口袋任务,GeoMem-VLA通过准确区分并操纵被拼接的堆叠配置中的目标文件口袋,实现了100%的成功率.
对于选择n倍立方体,挑战在于在反复的互动中保持进展. 政策需要记住,在适应当前情况的同时,完成了多少个成功的把握和位置周期。 时间记忆机制保存了重复操作中的任务进度,使GeoMem-VLA能够完成所需的互动数量.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
Inspired by the thought patterns of human action, we propose GeoMem-VLA to illustrate how humans conceptualize and store spatial information of the current scene in their minds as memory to guide action generation during decision-making.
This method allows spatial information learned through reconstruction to remain available as latent context throughout task execution.
LIBERO and RoboTwin results support its applicability across manipulation tasks.
Experiments on two physical robot platforms further cover precise spatial interaction, changing visibility, and multi-stage manipulation. These results support geometry-supervised latent memory as a practical connection between 3D representation learning and action generation over time, effectively improving VLA model’s decision-making ability.
blocks.zh:
受人类行动的思想规律所启发,我们提议GeoMem-VLA,以说明人类如何将当前场景的空间信息概念化并存储在脑中,作为记忆来指导决策过程中的行动生成.
这种方法使通过重建获得的空间信息在整个任务执行过程中仍可作为潜在背景提供。
LIBERO和RoboTwin成果支持它适用于操纵任务。
在两个物理机器人平台上的实验进一步涵盖了精确的空间相互作用,改变能见度,以及多相操纵. 这些结果支持了几何学监督的潜在记忆,作为三维表现学习和随时间推移产生行动之间的实际联系,有效地提高了VLA模型的决策能力.

blocks.en: We conduct real-world experiments on two dual-arm robot platforms, Astribot S1 and AgileX Cobot Magic 2, as shown in Figure 4 . These platforms provide different robot embodiments for evaluating the applicability of GeoMem-VLA in real-world manipulation scenarios.

blocks.en: The Astribot S1 is a dual-arm humanoid manipulation platform equipped with two 7-DoF arms and dexterous end-effectors. The robot is equipped with a three-camera visual system, including one head-mounted RGB camera and two wrist-mounted RGB cameras, which provide global scene observations and close-range views for manipulation.
blocks.zh: Astribot S1是一款双臂人造操控平台,配备有2个7-DoF臂和可破解的最终效应器. 该机器人配备了三相机的视觉系统,包括一款头架的RGB相机和两款手腕架的RGB相机,这些相机提供全局场景观测和近距离视角来进行操纵.

blocks.en: The AgileX Cobot Magic 2 is a dual-arm collaborative robot platform equipped with two 6-DoF robotic arms and parallel grippers. Similar to Astribot S1, it uses a three-camera configuration consisting of one head-mounted RGB camera and two wrist-mounted RGB cameras.
blocks.zh: AgileX Cobot Magic 2是一款双臂协作机器人平台,配备了两个6-DoF机器人臂和并列的抓取器. 与Astribot S1类似,它使用由一台头架RGB相机和两台手腕架RGB相机组成的三相机配置.

blocks.en: E.2 Task Description
blocks.zh: E.2 任务说明

blocks.en: We design five real-world manipulation tasks on two robot platforms to evaluate different aspects of GeoMem-VLA , including spatial understanding, object-level manipulation, and long-horizon task execution. The tasks cover diverse interaction patterns, ranging from precise object placement to sequential manipulation with changing task states.
blocks.zh: 我们在两个机器人平台上设计了五个真实世界的操纵任务,以评价GeoMem-VLA的不同方面,包括空间理解,对象水平操纵,以及长视距任务执行. 任务涵盖了不同的相互作用模式,从精确的对象定位到随任务状态变化而相继被操纵.

blocks.en: E.3 Evaluation Protocol
blocks.zh: E.3 评价议定书

blocks.en: For each real-world task, we conduct 10 independent evaluation rollouts under randomized initial configurations. Before each rollout, object positions are randomly initialized within the demonstrated workspace, while task-specific parameters (e.g., the target number in the pick n times cube task) are randomly assigned.
blocks.zh: 每项现实世界任务,我们都要在随机初步配置下进行10次独立评价。 在每次展开前,对象位置在所显示的工作空间内随机初始化,而任务特定参数(例如取出n乘以立方的任务中的目标数)则被随机指定.

blocks.en: During evaluation, the robot executes the policy in a closed-loop manner without external intervention. A rollout is considered successful only when the robot completes the entire task procedure and satisfies the predefined task objective. Partial completion of a task is counted as failure.
blocks.zh: 在评价期间,机器人在没有外部干预的情况下,以闭锁方式执行政策. 只有在机器人完成整个任务程序并满足预先确定的任务目标时,推出才被认为是成功的. 部分完成一项任务被算作失败.

blocks.en: E.4 Baseline Implementation
blocks.zh: E.4 基线执行情况

blocks.en: We compare GeoMem-VLA with three representative VLA baselines, including LingBot-VLA 2.0, π \pi 0.5, and OpenVLA-OFT. To ensure a fair comparison, all baselines are fine-tuned and evaluated following their official configurations and recommended training pipelines.
blocks.zh: 我们比较GeoMem-VLA与三个具有代表性的VLA基线,包括LingBot-VLA 2.0,π\pi 0.5和OpenVLA-OFT. 为确保公平比较,所有基线都按照官方配置和建议的培训管道进行微调和评价。

blocks.en: For each task, the baseline models are fine-tuned using the same task-specific demonstration data collected in our experiments. The adapted models are then evaluated under the same rollout settings, including identical initial configurations, evaluation episodes, and success criteria.
blocks.zh: 对于每项任务,都利用我们实验中收集的相同任务特定示范数据,对基准模型进行微调. 然后在同样的推出设置下对经过调整的模型进行评价,包括相同的初始配置、评价插播和成功标准。
